genai.q: Speech-to-speech model or a pipeline?
genai.a: Speech-to-speech gives the lowest latency and natural prosody; a pipeline gives more control over each component, language choices, and tool use. Many teams start with a platform that manages the pipeline.
genai.topic: AI Agents, MCP & APIs for PMs and BAs

genai.q: What are the risks of voice cloning?
genai.a: Impersonation and fraud, consent and IP issues, regulatory problems with undisclosed AI calls, and reputational damage; mitigate with consent, verification, disclosure and watermarking.
genai.topic: AI Agents, MCP & APIs for PMs and BAs

genai.q: How do you support Indian languages?
genai.a: Choose STT and TTS that handle Hindi, Hinglish and regional languages, test accents, allow code-switching, and keep prompts and knowledge in the caller's language.
genai.topic: AI Agents, MCP & APIs for PMs and BAs

genai.q: What is the business case for a voice agent?
genai.a: Cost per resolved call vs human agents, 24x7 availability, faster answer times, conversion uplift, minus platform, telephony and maintenance costs, with quality guardrails.
genai.topic: AI Agents, MCP & APIs for PMs and BAs

genai.q: Difference between AI, ML and generative AI?
genai.a: AI is the broad field; ML learns patterns from data to predict or classify; generative AI (a deep-learning subset) creates new content such as text, code and images.

genai.q: What is a hallucination and how do you reduce it?
genai.a: Confident but false output. Reduce it by grounding answers in provided documents or data (RAG), using tools that compute results, lowering temperature, asking for sources and assumptions, and verifying independently.

genai.q: How do you write a good prompt for a data task?
genai.a: State the role, context (schema, grain, definitions), a single clear task, the required output format, and constraints (use only given data, state assumptions); give examples; iterate.

genai.q: What is agentic AI?
genai.a: Systems where an LLM plans and executes multi-step tasks using tools, observes results and continues until a goal is met, with human oversight for risky actions.

genai.q: How would you use AI to speed up SQL work safely?
genai.a: Provide schema, definitions and dialect; generate and explain queries; review for grain, filters and definitions; run read-only with limits; reconcile totals; keep verified queries in a library.

genai.q: What is Docker and why is it useful for data tools?
genai.a: A container platform that packages apps with their dependencies so the same setup runs anywhere; useful to spin up Metabase, databases or Jupyter in one command and share reproducible environments.

genai.q: What are the risks of connecting an AI assistant to a database?
genai.a: Data exposure to a model provider, destructive queries, wrong answers presented as facts, and prompt injection; mitigate with read-only access to curated views, masking, review and logging.

genai.q: What is Metabase?
genai.a: An open-source BI tool where users can ask questions with a visual builder or SQL, build dashboards and share them, with permission control by group.

genai.q: How would you use AI tools to speed up Excel analysis responsibly?
genai.a: Prepare structured data, ask specific questions, review generated formulas and pivots, reconcile totals, document assumptions, keep sensitive data out of unapproved tools, and keep a human sign-off.

genai.q: What is Python in Excel?
genai.a: A feature that runs Python (pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn) in cells via =PY(), in a secure cloud, reading Excel ranges with xl(), useful for analysis and charts that are hard with formulas.

genai.q: What is an AI agent in an office context and what are its risks?
genai.a: A system that plans and executes multi-step tasks using apps and files; risks include wrong actions, data leakage, prompt injection and lack of audit; mitigate with scoped permissions, approvals, copies and logs.

genai.q: How do you check an AI-generated formula?
genai.a: Test on a few rows including edge cases, compare totals with a simple independent calculation, read the formula's explanation, and make sure references and units are right.

genai.q: Walk me through how you use AI in your analysis workflow.
genai.a: I frame the decision, give the AI a clear brief with schema and definitions, use it to draft and explain SQL or Python, run everything myself, reconcile totals and cross-check with a second method, use AI for chart and narrative drafts, then I validate each number and take responsibility for the recommendation.

genai.q: What is an AI agent and how is it different from a chatbot?
genai.a: A chatbot responds once to a prompt; an agent pursues a goal across multiple steps by calling tools, observing results and deciding what to do next, so it needs stronger guardrails and evaluation.

genai.q: How do you stop an AI analytics tool from giving wrong numbers?
genai.a: Governed semantic layer, read-only access to curated data, golden-question tests, execution-based evaluation, human review of important outputs, and logging.

genai.q: A model says "contract type drives churn". What do you say?
genai.a: The data shows an association; to claim causation we would need an experiment or a causal method, controlling for tenure and other factors.

genai.q: Explain how ChatGPT or Claude works to a business audience.
genai.a: It is a model trained on vast text to predict the next word-piece; that teaches it language and knowledge. Further training with example conversations and human feedback makes it follow instructions helpfully and safely. It does not look things up unless connected to tools or documents.

genai.q: What is a context window?
genai.a: The maximum number of tokens (prompt, history, documents, output) the model can consider in one request.

genai.q: How do you reduce hallucinations in a business application?
genai.a: Retrieval-augmented generation with citations, tool use for facts and numbers, instructions to say "I don't know", structured outputs with validation, evaluation sets and human review for high-stakes outputs.

genai.q: How do you make an LLM output reliable enough for production?
genai.a: Specific prompts with examples, structured outputs with schema validation, low randomness, retries on validation failure, grounding in provided data, evaluation sets, and monitoring.

genai.q: What is prompt injection and how do you mitigate it?
genai.a: User-supplied or retrieved text that tries to override instructions. Mitigate by separating data from instructions, limiting tool permissions, validating outputs, filtering inputs, and never letting the model take irreversible actions without checks.

genai.q: Zero-shot vs few-shot prompting?
genai.a: Zero-shot gives only instructions; few-shot adds worked examples, which usually improves consistency on format and edge cases.

genai.q: How would you estimate the cost of an LLM feature?
genai.a: Requests per day × (input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price), measured on real samples with token counting, then reduced with model choice, caching, batching and shorter outputs.

genai.q: How do you make LLM API calls robust?
genai.a: Timeouts, retries with exponential backoff for 429/5xx, validation of outputs, checking stop reasons, fallbacks (another model or a rule), idempotent processing and logging.

genai.q: How do you keep a long chatbot conversation within budget?
genai.a: Trim or summarise older turns, cache the stable system prompt, retrieve only relevant documents, and cap output length.

genai.q: What is an embedding and how is it used in search?
genai.a: A dense vector representing meaning. Documents are embedded once and stored; a query is embedded at search time, and the nearest document vectors (by cosine similarity) are returned, often combined with keyword search.

genai.q: How does HNSW work at a high level?
genai.a: It builds a layered graph where each vector links to near neighbours; search starts at a coarse top layer and greedily moves closer to the query through lower layers, visiting only a small part of the data.

genai.q: How do you evaluate a semantic search system?
genai.a: A labelled set of queries with relevant documents; measure recall@k, precision@k, MRR or nDCG, plus latency and cost, and compare keyword, vector and hybrid configurations.

genai.q: Explain RAG and when you would use it instead of fine-tuning.
genai.a: RAG retrieves relevant documents at question time and has the model answer from them; use it when knowledge is large, private or changing and you need citations. Fine-tuning suits behaviour, style or format, not frequently updated facts.

genai.q: How do you evaluate a RAG system?
genai.a: Separately: retrieval (hit rate, MRR, recall on labelled questions) and generation (correctness, faithfulness to sources, citation accuracy, abstention), plus latency and cost; use human review and LLM judges calibrated against humans.

genai.q: Your RAG bot gives wrong answers. How do you debug it?
genai.a: Inspect retrieved chunks for failing questions: if the right chunk is missing, fix chunking, retrieval or query rewriting; if present but the answer is wrong, re-rank, reduce noise, and tighten the prompt; add the cases to the test set.

genai.q: How does function calling work?
genai.a: You describe tools with JSON schemas; the model returns a structured tool call instead of text when it needs one; your code executes it and sends the result back; the model continues until it can answer.

genai.q: How do you stop an LLM agent from doing something harmful with tools?
genai.a: Least-privilege credentials, input validation and allow-lists, amount/rate limits, human approval for side effects, sandboxing, audit logs, and treating retrieved content as untrusted data.

genai.q: Tool use vs RAG?
genai.a: RAG retrieves text to read; tool use performs computations or actions and fetches live structured data. Many assistants combine both, with retrieval itself exposed as a tool.

genai.q: What is agentic AI and how is it different from generative AI?
genai.a: Generative AI produces content in response to a prompt; agentic AI uses models in a loop with tools and memory to pursue a goal across multiple steps, deciding what to do next.

genai.q: How would you design a reliable agent for business reporting?
genai.a: Narrow tools with read-only data access, a planning step, required tool-sourced numbers, an automated checker, human approval before distribution, step and cost limits, tracing, and an evaluation suite of past questions.

genai.q: When would you not use an agent?
genai.a: When a fixed workflow or single call solves the task, when errors are costly and hard to detect, or when latency and cost budgets are tight.

genai.q: Explain MCP and why it matters.
genai.a: An open protocol that standardises how AI assistants discover and call external tools and read data. Organisations build a server once and make internal systems available to any compliant assistant, with consistent security and governance.

genai.q: Tools vs resources in MCP?
genai.a: Tools perform actions or computations and are chosen by the model; resources are read-only data the application or user attaches as context.

genai.q: What are the main security risks of MCP and how do you mitigate them?
genai.a: Untrusted servers, tool poisoning, prompt injection via returned content, and over-privileged credentials; mitigate with vetted servers, least privilege, OAuth, user approval for side effects, input validation and audit logging.

genai.q: How do you evaluate a generative AI application?
genai.a: Define success criteria per task; build a representative and adversarial test set; use automated metrics where possible (exact match, execution accuracy, schema validity), rubric-based human or LLM-judge scores for open text, calibrate judges against humans, and run regressions on every change plus production monitoring.

genai.q: What guardrails would you put on a customer-facing chatbot?
genai.a: Input checks (length, scope, PII, injection), retrieval restricted to approved content, least-privilege tools with approval for refunds or account changes, output validation (schema, policy, grounded facts), refusal handling, logging with PII redaction, and human escalation.

genai.q: What is prompt injection and why is it hard to solve completely?
genai.a: Instructions hidden in user or retrieved content that hijack the model. Models process instructions and data in the same channel, so filters can be evaded; robust systems limit what a compromised model can do.

genai.q: RAG or fine-tuning?
genai.a: RAG for knowledge that changes or needs citations; fine-tuning for consistent behaviour, format, tone or narrow tasks at scale. They combine well: a fine-tuned model can still use RAG.

genai.q: Explain LoRA in one minute.
genai.a: Instead of updating a huge weight matrix, LoRA learns two small matrices whose product approximates the needed change; the original weights stay frozen, so training is cheap and adapters are small and swappable.

genai.q: How would you decide between an API model and a self-hosted model?
genai.a: Evaluate quality on the task, total monthly cost including engineering, latency, data-privacy and residency requirements, licence terms and the team's ability to operate GPUs.

genai.q: How would you build a "chat with your data" tool safely?
genai.a: Curated read-only views with documented columns and metric definitions, schema-aware prompts, guarded execution with timeouts and row limits, show the SQL and results to the user, evaluate with a gold question set, log queries, and route ambiguous questions to analysts.

genai.q: What are the risks of AI-generated analysis code?
genai.a: Silent logic errors, wrong joins and definitions, security issues, and data leakage to external tools; mitigate with tests, reconciliation checks, code review and approved tools.

genai.q: How can LLMs help with data cleaning?
genai.a: Normalising categories and entity names, extracting structured fields from text, detecting anomalies in descriptions, and generating cleaning code, always with validation against allowed values and source data.

genai.q: How would you take an LLM prototype to production?
genai.a: Add evaluation and regression tests, guardrails, authentication and rate limits, observability, cost and latency budgets, privacy compliance, gradual rollout with monitoring, and clear human escalation.

genai.q: How do you control the cost of a chatbot?
genai.a: Model routing, prompt caching, concise retrieval, output limits, summarised history, batching offline work and dashboards with alerts on cost per conversation.

genai.q: What would you monitor after launch?
genai.a: Quality (feedback, judge scores), safety (guardrail hits, refusals), cost, latency, errors and drift in user questions.

genai.q: How do you keep designs consistent across a large product?
genai.a: A shared library of components with variants and properties, styles and variables (tokens) with modes, documentation pages, and Dev Mode / Code Connect so code uses the same tokens.

genai.q: Auto layout vs constraints?
genai.a: Auto layout arranges children in a flow (direction, gap, padding, hug/fill), like flexbox; constraints pin a layer to its parent's edges when the parent is resized, for frames without auto layout.

genai.q: How do you use Figma as a PM or analyst?
genai.a: Wireframe flows and dashboards, run FigJam workshops, review prototypes with users before building, comment on designs, and prototype quickly with Figma Make.

genai.q: n8n vs Zapier vs Make?
genai.a: Zapier is the simplest for app-to-app automations; Make adds visual branching and data mapping; n8n adds self-hosting, full code steps, sub-workflows and strong AI-agent features, which suits data and AI teams.

genai.q: How do you make an automation reliable?
genai.a: Retries with backoff, error branches and an error workflow with alerts, idempotent steps (check before creating), rate-limit batching, logging executions, separate test and production, and secrets in credentials.

genai.q: How would you build a support bot on company documents in n8n?
genai.a: An indexing workflow that loads documents, splits them, embeds them and stores them in a vector store; a chat workflow with Chat Trigger, an AI Agent with a chat model, memory and the vector store as a retrieval tool, with sources in answers and a human-handover path.

genai.q: When should you NOT use AI for a feature?
genai.a: “When a simple rule or search works reliably; when errors are costly and can't be caught; when we lack authorised data; when latency or cost exceeds the value; when we can't evaluate quality. Always compare with a non-AI baseline.”

genai.q: Explain RAG vs fine-tuning.
genai.a: “RAG retrieves current, permitted knowledge at answer time — good for facts, citations and fast updates. Fine-tuning adjusts behaviour or format using training examples — good for consistent style or specialised tasks. Neither guarantees truth; they can be combined.” *(Module 10.)*

genai.q: How would you evaluate an LLM-powered support bot before launch?
genai.a: “Build a curated eval set (common, edge, adversarial, escalation cases); score correctness, groundedness, safety and policy compliance with a rubric; use human review and a validated LLM judge; weight failures by severity; set launch gates; pilot with human-in-the-loop; then track online metrics.”

genai.q: Your AI feature hallucinates 3% of the time. Launch or not?
genai.a: “Depends on harm: 3% wrong recipe ideas may be fine with labels; 3% wrong policy answers in banking is not. Reduce with grounding and refusals, route high-risk intents to humans, show citations, and measure severity, not just rate.”

genai.q: How do you estimate the cost of an LLM feature?
genai.a: “Input and output tokens per request times prices times volume, plus retrieval, retries and multi-step calls; compare with value per request. Levers: smaller models for simple intents, caching, shorter prompts. Example: ~$0.0105 per answer at hypothetical prices.” *(Module 10.)*

genai.q: Design an AI feature for an e-commerce app.
genai.a: “Focus on finding the right product for a need: semantic search plus review summaries grounded in actual reviews with links; evaluate summary accuracy before launch; measure descriptive-search conversion and returns; manage risks of hallucinated claims and seller fairness.” *(Case 3; Lecture 40 ideas were proposals to validate.)*

genai.q: What metrics would you track for a generative AI assistant?
genai.a: “Business outcome (resolution, time saved), UX (CSAT, re-asks), quality (correctness, groundedness, citation accuracy), safety (policy violations, leaks), system (p95 latency, cost per request).”

genai.q: Tell me about an AI project you worked on.
genai.a: “Structure: user problem → why AI → data sources and permissions → architecture (retrieval, model, tools) → evaluation method and results (real, or ‘not measured’) → risks and controls → my contribution → what I'd do next.” *(Lecture 52: a POC is not a delivered outcome.)*

genai.q: What is the difference between an LLM, a chatbot and an AI agent?
genai.a: An LLM is the model that predicts text; a chatbot is an interface that lets people talk to it; an agent wraps a model with instructions, tools, memory and a loop so it can take multi-step actions toward a goal.

genai.q: How do you reduce hallucinations in a production AI feature?
genai.a: Ground answers in retrieved sources (RAG) with citations, ask for 'I don't know' when context is missing, constrain outputs with schemas, evaluate on a labelled test set, and add human review for high-impact answers.

genai.q: How would you estimate the monthly cost of an LLM feature?
genai.a: Requests per month x (input tokens x input price + output tokens x output price), plus embeddings and infrastructure; reduce with caching, smaller models for simple turns, shorter prompts and output limits.

genai.q: What is the role of evaluation sets in GenAI products?
genai.a: They are the regression tests of AI: real, labelled examples that measure accuracy, groundedness, safety and tone before every prompt, model or data change ships.

other.q: How would you grow a brand's LinkedIn presence?
other.a: Founder- and employee-led posts with stories and lessons, a consistent weekly cadence, carousels and short videos, engaging with relevant creators, employee advocacy, and measuring follower growth, engagement and inbound leads.

other.q: How do you decide what content to make next?
other.a: Audience questions (comments, DMs, search data), top-performing past posts, competitor gaps, and the business goal for the month.

other.q: Short-form or long-form?
other.a: Short builds reach and discovery; long builds trust and depth; most creators use short to bring people to long and to owned channels like newsletters.

other.q: How do you use AI without sounding generic?
other.a: Feed it your own examples and voice, use it for structure and editing, add personal stories and data, and always edit the final version yourself.

other.q: How do you price a brand deal?
other.a: Based on average views/reach, engagement, niche value, deliverables, usage rights and exclusivity, with a media kit and a written agreement.

other.q: Why do you want to be an FDE?
other.a: Show that you enjoy owning real outcomes, working with customers and building end to end, with a story where you solved a messy real-world problem.

other.q: A customer's data is messy and access is delayed. What do you do?
other.a: Get a representative sample under an NDA or in a secure environment, build a thin slice with synthetic or masked data, document blockers with owners and dates, and escalate early with the business impact.

other.q: How do you decide whether to build custom or wait for the product?
other.a: Weigh customer value and urgency, how many other customers need it, maintenance cost, and whether it can be built as a reusable component; agree with the product team.

other.q: Design an AI assistant for a support team with strict compliance.
other.a: Read-only tools first, RAG with citations, PII redaction, human approval for outgoing messages, audit logs, evaluation on labelled cases, data residency and provider data policies, and a staged rollout.

other.q: How do you show the value of a deployment?
other.a: Agree baseline and target metrics upfront, instrument usage and outcomes, report weekly, and translate improvements into money, time or risk reduced.

other.q: Your CPL doubled last week. What do you check?
other.a: Tracking changes, auction/competition and CPMs, creative fatigue (frequency, CTR drop), audience or budget changes, landing page speed or errors, and seasonality; then fix the biggest driver.

other.q: SEO vs paid search?
other.a: SEO builds compounding, lower-cost traffic over months; paid search buys immediate, controllable intent. Most brands run both and share keyword insights.

other.q: How do you measure brand campaigns?
other.a: Reach and frequency, brand-search lift, direct traffic, brand-lift studies, and incrementality or MMM, not last-click conversions alone.

other.q: What is a good landing page?
other.a: Message match with the ad, one goal, clear value and proof, simple form, fast mobile load, and a tested CTA.

other.q: How do you use AI responsibly in marketing?
other.a: For research, drafts and variants with human review, fact-checking, brand and legal compliance, consent-based data, and disclosure of synthetic media.

other.q: Data extension vs list?
other.a: Lists hold subscribers with basic attributes and are simple; data extensions are custom tables with your own fields and keys, faster at scale and needed for SQL, relational data and most journeys.

other.q: How do you prevent sending to the wrong audience?
other.a: Use verified SQL with counts, a Verification activity, suppression/exclusion DEs, test sends against testable DEs, approvals, and send classifications that respect unsubscribes.

other.q: How do you improve deliverability?
other.a: Authenticate the domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), warm up IPs, clean lists, segment for engagement, honour unsubscribes quickly, keep complaint rates low and monitor bounces.

other.q: Journey Builder entry sources?
other.a: Data extension, API event, Salesforce data via Marketing Cloud Connect, CloudPages forms, and audiences from Data Cloud.

other.q: How would you measure a journey?
other.a: Entry volume, step conversion, goal completion, revenue per contact, time to convert, unsubscribe and complaint rates, compared with a hold-out group.
